readout: Deaminase activity after 1 generation(s) of rifampin selection, as the deposit's enrichment score; higher is more active
assay_method: Sat-Sel-Seq: a cassette-mutagenesis library of human AID with NNS degenerate codons at the target codon and a silent mutation in the next codon as a barcode, expressed in Escherichia coli together with uracil-DNA glycosylase inhibitor and selected for rifampin resistance. Functioning AID deaminates the rpoB gene, producing rifampin-resistant hosts, so growth reports deaminase activity. Initial and selected counts per variant were determined by 454 pyrosequencing. Per-variant scores were taken from the authors' MaveDB deposit.
remark: The sequence is UniProt Q9GZX7 exactly, 198 aa, and every label verifies against it, but the library covers only positions 113-123, 11 codons of the 198, so 187 residues carry no variant and rest on provenance alone. 11 nonsense rows are dropped, a premature stop not being writable as a substitution. Their median of 0.141 sits below the substitutions' 0.580, which is how the orientation of the deposit's score was checked: a dead deaminase should not confer rifampin resistance, and it does not, so the score is used as it stands. The deposit writes its wild-type measurements in substitution form as p.XnnX rather than with '=', so the 11 of them are the wild-type protein and collapse to the single WT row at their mean. The deposit's three score sets are generation 1, 2 and 3 of iterative selection on the same library and are three datasets, not one: selection sharpens with each round, the median falling 0.580 to 0.227 to 0.073 while the maximum rises 8.5 to 21.0, and consecutive generations correlate at r = 0.773 and 0.971 rather than being reuploads.
